scenarios.evidence: Focused workspace tests with a real Git fixture, a spaced `KOGEN_WORKSPACES_ROOT`, a real-root sentinel directory, a foreign worktree and a launch sentinel assert the paths, branch, owner record fields, base commit, deps copy, absence of `_build/`, Approved bytes, byte-identical control state, and each refusal case with no launch.
scenarios.given: A clean control checkout attached to branch B at commit A, with control `deps/` and `_build/` present, a frozen Approved package in control's ignored `.kogen/intents/approved/<slug>/`, and an unrelated linked worktree created by plain git (for example under `.kogen/runtime/build-worktrees/`).

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: real git worktree fixture with foreign-worktree, collision, missing-deps, real-root-sentinel and launch-sentinel controls; no provider semantics

scenarios.then: Before any provider launch, exactly one new linked worktree exists at `<workspaces-root>/<project-id>/<slug>-<build-id>/` on new branch `kogen/<slug>/<build-id>` at A, where `<project-id>` equals `Kogen.ClaudeCode.project_id(control)` and `<build-id>` is the scenario-tracking record id. The harness home `<workspaces-root>/<project-id>/harness/<build-id>/` exists outside the Candidate and outside control. The owner record `<workspaces-root>/<project-id>/candidates/<build-id>.json` has status `running` and names the worktree, branch, admitted commit, control root, harness home and credential bindings. The Candidate has a plain copy of control `deps/`, no `_build/`, and the Approved bytes at its ignored `.kogen/intents/approved/<slug>/`. Control's HEAD, index, tracked bytes and `git status --porcelain` are unchanged, the foreign worktree is untouched, and a sentinel real Kogen root stays empty. A pre-existing path, branch or owner record with that name, a missing control `deps/` (message names `mix deps.get`), or a failed `git worktree add` stops before any launch, removes only what this admission created, and never falls back to control.
scenarios.when: `mix kogen.build <slug>` is admitted with `KOGEN_WORKSPACES_ROOT` set to a directory whose path contains a space.
scenarios.wrong_result: Build keeps running in the invoking checkout, nests the worktree in the repository, writes under the real Kogen directory while `KOGEN_WORKSPACES_ROOT` is set, copies `_build/`, reuses an existing directory or branch, fetches dependencies from the network, or deletes a foreign worktree during admission.

scenarios.evidence: Offline: claude_code_management_test.exs asserts the environment of the Shape terminal, login and status launches (each with an inherited empty `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` planted), harness_home_test.exs asserts the Build's Claude deltas and that the fake `claude auth status` readiness call receives the Build's own environment before the first model launch, and codex_environment_test.exs asserts the Codex deltas and operation-root location; fake-harness Builds record every launch's `HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME`, flip the selector mid-Build, snapshot the scope directory's file list before and after, put a recording fake `security` first on PATH to assert it is never invoked by Kogen code, and run two Builds in sequence with a planted marker. Paid: live_shape_to_build_test.exs asserts the transcript locations and the binding named in `then`, using RootProfileAudit.sessions_root(fixture), which must cover both the scope and the project's harness homes.
scenarios.given: A control project whose Claude Code login selector names a scope (shared or project), a Codex login scope, and a caller environment that sets `HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` (to an empty string), `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CODEX_HOME` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

proof.paid_reason: provider-required: live-shape-to-build; observation: the managed Claude Code runtime authenticates a real Developer, and resumes its session, from a per-Build CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR through CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR pointing at the Shape session's scope, with the real Keychain; offline-limit: a fake harness cannot show that the real runtime resolves the Keychain item and refresh lock from the reference instead of the config dir

scenarios.then: Every Claude Code launch of the Build has `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` equal to `<harness home>/claude`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` equal to the scope path resolved from the control root at admission, and the caller's real `HOME`; every variable that `Kogen.ClaudeCode.environment/2` removes at 2909f557 (the `ANTHROPIC_`, `CLAUDE_CODE_`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDECODE` prefixes, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `VERTEX_REGION_CLAUDE`), the Codex adapter's blocked prefixes (`CODEX_`, `OPENAI_`, `AZURE_`, `CHATGPT_`, so an inherited `OPENAI_API_KEY` cannot fund a Claude role's shell) and the inherited `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` is absent or replaced, asserted in the environment the launched child process actually sees. Every Codex launch has `CODEX_HOME` equal to its scope, its operation root (private `HOME`, `XDG_*`, sqlite) under `<harness home>/codex`, and every variable in Codex's existing blocked set (including `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) removed. Readiness ran with the Build's own launch environment before any model launch. The switched selector does not change any later launch of the running Build. The owner record and tracking record name each binding (harness, scope name and path, runtime version). A Claude scope directory's file list is identical before and after a fake Build, and a Codex scope differs at most by the two deterministic files Kogen already maintains there (`environments.toml`, `agents/kogen_boundary.toml`), pre-seeded in the fixture; no credential file in either scope is created, copied, linked, moved, renamed or rewritten by Kogen, no Kogen code path invokes `security` or opens a credential file, and a marker written into one Build's harness home is absent from a second Build's launch environment and home. Every other Kogen Claude Code launch (Shape, login, status) sets `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` equal to its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, overriding an inherited value. In the real fixture, the Build's Developer transcript (with its session id from the tracking record) exists under `<harness home>/claude/projects/` and not under the scope's `projects/`, the Developer completed a turn and a resume there, the tracking record's Claude binding names the scope path, and the Shape session's transcripts are under that scope's `projects/`.
scenarios.when: A Build is admitted and launches its Claude Code Developer, a resume and helpers, and its Reviewer on the route's harness; during the Build the project's login selector is switched with `mix kogen.claude.login --use-default` or `--project`.
scenarios.wrong_result: A private `HOME` is set for Claude Code and every role reports not logged in; a fresh `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is used without the secure-storage reference; the credential file or Keychain item is copied into the harness home; the scope is keyed on the Candidate path or re-resolved per launch so a mid-Build selector change switches logins; or an inherited empty `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` is left in place and the personal login is used.

scenarios.evidence: Each fake harness (`fake_claude*`, `fake_codex*`) writes, from inside the launched process, its `pwd -P` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to a per-launch receipt, so the assertion is on the OS process state, not on launch arguments or environment. The fake-harness lifecycle asserts those receipts, the report's changed paths, selector checks and packet against the Candidate-only sentinel, with a control-only sentinel as the negative control, and runs one Build from a third cwd whose own sentinel must never appear.
scenarios.given: An admitted Build whose control checkout and Candidate hold different sentinel files, a Candidate edit that adds a proof selector file and changes a guarded path, a control-only edit to an ignored file, and a controller process whose cwd is a third directory.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: fake-harness lifecycle with control and Candidate sentinels and a third-directory cwd control; the real-provider cwd is covered by same-candidate-rework

scenarios.then: Every role launch (Claude and Codex adapters) has cwd and Git toplevel equal to the Candidate, and Codex trusts the Candidate as its project root. Candidate id, changed paths, guarded-path capture, proof-selector existence, report entries, review packet contents, citation snapshots, staging and commit are computed from the Candidate root passed explicitly: the Candidate-only selector counts as present and the control-only edit never appears. Lock, tracking record, verification context, state, history and receipts, prompts, route and config, and login-scope identity stay on the control root passed explicitly. `Harness.open`, both adapters' `open`, `VerificationPolicy.preflight/2`, `VerificationPolicy.environment`, `GuardedPaths.capture`, `Git.changed_paths`, `VerificationPlan.load/build/missing_selectors` and `Build.Evidence.resolve` receive their root explicitly from Build (no `File.cwd!()` or `"."` default is used on any Build path), and a Build started from the third directory behaves identically. `KOGEN_TASK_CONTEXT` `working_directory` names the Candidate. Ordinary citations are Candidate-relative; the tracking-record citation and `build-summary.json` `full_record.path` resolve from control.
scenarios.when: The controller runs the fresh Developer, its controller verification, the report, the review packet and Jev, an exact-session resume, and each fresh Reviewer.
scenarios.wrong_result: Roles run in the Candidate but the report says "no changes", or a missing selector looks present, because Git and file checks still read control; the Codex Reviewer trusts control and ignores the Candidate's project files; or a fallback `File.cwd!()` hides a missing root.

scenarios.evidence: A controller test with a fixture whose control passes and Candidate fails asserts the failed receipt, the Candidate id and the resumed session, and repeats it with tampered Candidate hook copies. A byte-comparison test asserts the three hook and settings paths are unchanged from the admission commit and that the PreToolUse registration matches.
scenarios.given: A fixture project whose control `make check` passes, and a fixture Intent whose `may_change_guarded_paths` includes `.codex/hooks/**`, so that the Developer's turn leaves the Candidate's `make check` failing and its copies of `.codex/hooks/check.sh`, `stop_runner.py` and `verification_policy.py` edited to always pass or allow. A second fixture Intent does not guard `.codex/hooks/**`.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: the controller runs real Make targets in a fixture with a passing control and a failing, hook-tampered Candidate; the verdict path has no provider semantics

scenarios.then: The parent controller runs `make check` and each selected target with cwd equal to the Candidate, records a failed receipt bound to the Candidate id, and resumes the same Developer session through the normal retry path. The tampered hook copies change no receipt or verdict. With the second fixture Intent the same tampering stops the Build on the guarded-path check before any verification, as today. Build calls `VerificationPolicy.preflight(targets, candidate_root)` with the Candidate root explicitly. After this Intent's own Candidate, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.codex/hooks/**` and `priv/kogen/claude_code/settings.json` are byte-identical to the admission commit, and the registered PreToolUse command still equals the `@hook_command` main's controller compares against.
scenarios.when: The Developer's turn ends and the controller settles verification.
scenarios.wrong_result: The controller runs targets in control or in `File.cwd!()` and a failing Candidate passes on control's clean tree; or the Candidate rewrites the hook commands or Claude settings to "run from control", which main's controller then refuses at the next launch, as in Build cFnHwg7P2oNe1wMMnK7jxeMH.

scenarios.evidence: The fake lifecycle's per-launch receipts (written by the fake harness from inside each launched process: `pwd -P`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, session id) assert one Candidate, one harness home and one Developer session id across both resumptions and a distinct Reviewer session per Review, and the worktree list shows a single Candidate throughout. The live fixture's `KOGEN_WORKSPACES_ROOT` path contains a space; the live test reads the Candidate path from the tracking record's `candidate` block and asserts the cwd recorded in the Developer transcript (both turns) and in the Reviewer's native session equals it, plus the single Developer session id, controller receipts bound to the Candidate id, the final fixture HEAD, and that the worktree and branch are gone.
scenarios.given: A Build on the default route whose first controller verification fails and whose first Review requests rework.

proof.paid_reason: provider-required: live-shape-to-build; observation: a real Claude Code Developer resumes its exact session in a Candidate worktree cwd after a controller-failed verification, the real Reviewer runs there, and publication fast-forwards the fixture main; offline-limit: fake harnesses cannot show that the managed runtimes find and resume a session from a worktree cwd with a per-Build config dir

scenarios.then: In the fake lifecycle, the Developer, both resumes and both Reviewers run with cwd equal to the same single Candidate and use the same harness home; no second worktree or harness home is created; both resumes carry the first session id; each Review is a new Reviewer session; and the outer-attempt and verification-retry counters equal those two_outer_resumptions_test expects today. In the real fixture Build (which exercises a controller-failed verification and its resume, not a Review rework), the Claude Code Developer's transcript records the Candidate path as its cwd for both the first turn and the resumed turn under one session id, the real Reviewer session on the default route's Reviewer harness (Codex once cross-harness-adversarial-roles has landed, otherwise Claude Code) records the same Candidate cwd in its native session metadata, the fixture's main is fast-forwarded to the Intent commit, and no Candidate worktree or branch remains.

scenarios.wrong_result: Each outer attempt creates a new worktree and loses the Developer's edits; resume runs in another cwd or config dir where Claude Code cannot find the session; or the Reviewer reads control instead of the Candidate.

scenarios.evidence: Offline publication tests assert the commit parent is A, control status after the fast-forward, removal of the Approved copy, worktree, branch and owner record, the kept harness home, the untracked-file refusal, and fault injection before the fast-forward.
scenarios.given: An accepted Candidate while control is clean, attached to B, and B is still at A.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: real git fixtures for commit, fast-forward, synchronization and cleanup; the real publication is also observed by same-candidate-rework's live run

scenarios.then: One commit with the Intent title, source changes and Complete package is created in the Candidate under today's size limits, `.kogen/runtime/` rejection, index-flag refusal, trailers and commit hooks. B is fast-forwarded to it with control's index and working tree synchronized, and control's HEAD, tree and clean status are asserted. Control's ignored Approved copy of this slug is removed. The Candidate worktree is removed without `--force`, the branch with `git branch -d`, and the owner record is deleted; the harness home is kept. `git worktree list` is back to its pre-Build entries. `build-summary.json` and `evidence.md` resolve the full record from control. No merge commit, rebase or re-verification happens. If worktree removal is refused after the fast-forward (for example the Candidate holds an untracked file), B stays published, the Candidate worktree, branch and owner record are kept with owner status `published: cleanup refused: <reason>` and the tracking record's disposition `published-retained`, the Build exits zero with a warning that names the path and `mix kogen.candidates.remove <build-id>`, and that command later removes it without `--discard-accepted` because the commit is reachable from B.
scenarios.wrong_result: It commits in control from Candidate bytes; updates the ref with `update-ref` and leaves control's index stale; force-removes a Candidate holding untracked files; leaves the branch behind; or deletes the harness home before the transcripts can be audited.

scenarios.evidence: Offline tests cover each refusal cause and fault injection between the checks and the fast-forward, asserting refs, control bytes, the retained Candidate and the exact message fields.
scenarios.given: An accepted Candidate while B has moved, control is dirty, or control is on another branch.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: real git fixtures for moved-branch, dirty-control and other-branch refusals with retained-Candidate and message assertions

scenarios.then: B, control's index, working tree and ignored Approved package are unchanged. The Candidate worktree, branch (with the accepted commit) and harness home are kept. The Build exits non-zero with a message naming the reason, admitted and current commits, worktree path, branch, Candidate commit, tracking record and `mix kogen.candidates.remove <build-id> --discard-accepted`. The tracking record's `candidate.disposition` is `retained`, and the owner record's status is `accepted-unpublished: <reason>` with the Candidate commit.
scenarios.wrong_result: It publishes because the fast-forward happens to apply over non-overlapping dirty edits; merges or rebases onto the moved main; or discards the accepted commit.

scenarios.evidence: Fake-lifecycle stops for each category assert the retained paths, message and record fields, then run a second Build and assert distinct Candidates and homes and the untouched earlier one.
scenarios.given: Builds stopped by verification exhaustion, outer-allowance exhaustion, a Jev cannot-comply stop, an integrity failure, a provider failure and a malformed Review.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: fake-lifecycle stop categories with retained-Candidate and second-Build controls

scenarios.then: Each stopped Build keeps its Candidate worktree, branch and harness home unchanged. The stop message names the slug, build id, worktree path and branch next to the tracking record path, plus `mix kogen.candidates.remove <build-id>`. The record's `candidate.disposition` is `retained` and the owner record's status is `stopped: <category>`. Control is unchanged and the Approved package stays in control. The new Build creates a new Candidate and harness home and never adopts, reuses or deletes a retained one or any foreign worktree.
scenarios.when: Each Build stops, and afterwards a new Build of the same Intent is started.
scenarios.wrong_result: A stop deletes the Candidate and loses the evidence; the message omits it; or the next Build reuses the old worktree or harness home and inherits its edits or sessions.

scenarios.evidence: A fake-harness Build whose fake Developer, mid-turn, triggers the control-side writes asserts acceptance and publication, the untouched other packages, and two negative controls: an own-package mutation in the Candidate and a tracked edit in control.
scenarios.given: A running Build of slug S, and a control checkout in which, while the Developer's turn is in progress, another session writes a new Draft under `.kogen/intents/drafts/`, edits another Draft, moves another package into `.kogen/intents/approved/`, and runs a fake Shape session against the same login scope.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: real two-project git fixtures with running-lock, accepted-unpublished, foreign-worktree and owner-record mismatch controls

scenarios.then: List shows only P's Candidates with build id, slug, title, status (the stale one as `stopped: interrupted`), start time, branch and path. Remove deletes a stopped Candidate's worktree, branch, harness home and owner record; refuses the running one. For a Candidate holding a commit, the matrix is exact: commit reachable from the admitted branch (for example after the Shaper fast-forwarded it, or `published: cleanup refused`) is removed without a flag; commit not reachable is refused without `--discard-accepted` and removed with it. Remove refuses an id that is not P's, and a path that does not match its owner record or is not registered in P's `git worktree list`. Q's Candidate, the running Candidate and the foreign worktree survive. Each command prints what it removed or refused.
scenarios.when: From P the Shaper runs `mix kogen.candidates` and `mix kogen.candidates.remove <id>`, with and without `--discard-accepted`.
scenarios.wrong_result: List shows every project's worktrees or unnamed git paths; or remove deletes another project's Candidate, a foreign worktree, a running Candidate or an accepted commit without the flag.
